rules.rationale: Source ESOL prior: short SMILES gave +6.89 effect; small solutes transfer as easier-to-solvate molecules.
Source prior for smiles_mid was -6.61; moderate size added nonpolar bulk reducing solvation.
Strongest source prior (-11.46) at smiles_long; large hydrophobic bulk dominates cavity-formation cost.
Ring role carried highest transfer weight (0.758); acyclic solutes are typically less hydrophobic than ring-rich analogs.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers ESOL size and ring structure effects to FreeSolv hydration, assuming solubility and hydration share hydrophobic-bulk mechanics. Fails if hydration is driven by polar group count rather than molecular size.

rules.rationale: Many N/O heteroatoms enable hydrogen bonding with water, the dominant favorable term in hydration free energy.
Heavy halogenation gives low-polarity, hydrophobic surfaces with poor water hydrogen bonding and high cavity cost.
Moderate polarity without halogens is the classic hydrophilic small-solute regime in aqueous solvation datasets.
Counter-hypothesis: reverses the low-confidence ESOL size prior, since longer polar chains can add hydrating functional groups.

skills.hypothesis: Assumes hydration affinity tracks polar hydrogen-bonding capacity and penalizes halogenated hydrophobes, downweighting the uncertain ESOL size prior. Fails if the score instead rewards small nonpolar solutes.

fixed_initial.lesson: Cross-property transfer from ESOL solubility carries low source confidence (0.16-0.41) and only field-level roles, so mechanistic polarity rules are a safer prior than borrowed size effects.
fixed_initial.revision_summary: Kept the source-grounded size/ring transfer as one skill with values matched exactly to shared_value_priors, and added a counter-hypothesis skill that reverses the smiles_mid penalty and instead scores heteroatom-driven hydrogen bonding against halogen hydrophobicity. Selected the polarity skill for deployment; both use decaying semantic mass so target-only GP evidence dominates late.

rules.rationale: Multiple N/O sites both donate and accept water hydrogen bonds, the dominant favorable hydration term.
Moderate heteroatom content still supplies hydrogen-bonding functionality without excessive nonpolar bulk.
Pure hydrocarbons hydrate poorly; cavity formation in water's network dominates with no compensating hydrogen bonds.
Heavily halogenated surfaces are polarizable but weak hydrogen bonders, raising net desolvation cost.

skills.hypothesis: Hydration affinity tracks hydrogen-bonding capacity minus hydrophobic cavity cost, so heteroatom-rich, weakly halogenated solutes rank highest. Fails if the score rewards halogen bonding or nonpolar burial.

rules.rationale: Acyclic solutes expose less rigid nonpolar surface; source ring role carried the highest transfer weight, 0.758.
Flat aromatic faces are hydrophobic; their absence reduces cavity work in aqueous solvation.
Counter-hypothesis: reverses the low-confidence 0.22 ESOL size prior, since longer chains can add hydrating groups.
Heavy branching builds compact nonpolar cores that shield polar sites from water contact.

skills.hypothesis: Scaffold topology, not size, drives hydration: acyclic non-aromatic low-branch solutes gain while the weak ESOL size penalty is reversed. Fails if polar functionality dominates topology.

true_feedback.lesson: Across two development generations the polarity/hydrogen-bonding skill led on mean rank AUC (72.9 then 67.9) while size-transfer and scaffold-shape variants stayed near 54-56; sparse bins like aromatic_high and ring_token_high (2-3 candidates) contributed almost no usable signal. Evidence is directional from few seeds, not causal.
true_feedback.revision_summary: Kept the winning polar mechanism but replaced the sparse two-condition interaction with a broader hetero_mid main effect, so rules cover well-populated bins (28/91/207/43 candidates) instead of rare ones. The second skill drops the near-empty aromatic_high and ring_token_high penalties that underperformed and instead rewards the large acyclic and non-aromatic populations while explicitly reversing the low-confidence 0.22 ESOL size prior. Both keep decaying semantic mass; the polar skill is frozen for deployment.

rules.rationale: ESOL value prior: smiles_short gave +6.89 effect; compact solutes pay a smaller water cavity-formation cost.
Source prior for smiles_mid was -6.61; added nonpolar bulk raises the hydrophobic hydration penalty.
Strongest source value prior (-11.46) at smiles_long; a large hydrophobic surface dominates unfavorable solvation.
Ring field had the highest transfer weight (0.758); acyclic solutes are typically less hydrophobic than ring-rich analogs.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers ESOL size and ring-structure effects to hydration, assuming both properties share hydrophobic-bulk mechanics. Fails if hydration affinity is driven by polar hydrogen-bonding groups rather than molecular size.

rules.rationale: Abundant N/O centers give strong solute-water hydrogen bonding, the dominant favorable term in hydration free energy.
Heavily halogenated surfaces are weakly polar, hydrogen-bond poor, and incur large cavity costs in water.
Moderate polarity without halogens is the classic hydrophilic small-solute regime in aqueous solvation data.
Counter-hypothesis reversing the low-confidence ESOL size prior: longer chains often carry extra hydrating functional groups.

skills.hypothesis: Assumes hydration affinity tracks polar hydrogen-bonding capacity and penalizes halogenated hydrophobes, downweighting the uncertain ESOL size prior. Fails if the score instead rewards small nonpolar solutes.

no_feedback.lesson: Cross-property ESOL transfer carries low source confidence (0.16-0.41) and mostly field-level roles, so mechanistic hydrogen-bonding rules are a safer prior than borrowed size effects.
no_feedback.revision_summary: No development feedback was available, so both skills were re-derived from the supplied source evidence and schema. The ESOL size/ring arm is retained as the source-grounded transfer hypothesis, and the polarity arm combines domain knowledge (heteroatom hydrogen bonding versus halogen hydrophobicity) with a counter-hypothesis reversing the smiles_mid penalty. The polarity skill is selected for deployment; both decay semantic mass so the target-only GP anchor dominates in later rounds.

rules.rationale: Source prior for smiles_short was +6.89 with the largest support (261); small solutes pay the least cavity-formation work.
Source prior -11.46 at smiles_long; large nonpolar volume adds cavity cost faster than it adds favorable contacts.
Dense N/O substitution supports hydrogen bonding that partly offsets cavity cost, so polarity marks hydratable solutes.
Aromatic-rich solutes expose extended flat nonpolar surfaces with poor water contacts, matching the weak hydrophilic regime.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers the ESOL size ordering plus a mild polarity and aromatic-surface correction, assuming hydration is dominated by solute bulk with a secondary polar term. Fails if top candidates are polar and mid-length, or if the smiles_long prior reflects solubility mechanics that do not carry over.

rules.rationale: Retained compact-solute term: cavity work scales with molecular volume, the most transferable physical driver.
Counter-hypothesis: smiles_mid carried the lowest source confidence (0.27), so its penalty is neutralized rather than trusted.
Hydrocarbon-only solutes have no hydrogen-bonding term to offset cavity cost, the least favorable hydration regime.
Branch role transferred strongly (0.758); unbranched solutes bury less nonpolar surface and solvate more favorably.

skills.hypothesis: Downweights the mid-length prior and scores polarity absence against unbranched geometry, leaning harder on target-only GP rank evidence. Fails if the mid-length penalty is genuinely strong or if apolar hydrocarbon solutes are actually favored.

shuffled_feedback.lesson: Across both development blocks the size-grounded skill beat its counter-hypothesis partner (72.9 vs 54.3, then 57.9 vs 50.8), but the second block dropped roughly 15 AUC points, so the transfer signal is real yet seed-fragile and should be paired with a target-only fallback rather than trusted outright.
shuffled_feedback.revision_summary: Kept one source-grounded skill on the high-support smiles_short prior while trimming the least-supported smiles_long penalty from -0.55 to -0.4, and added two mechanistic rules with no source counterpart (hetero_high polar hydration, aromatic_high nonpolar surface penalty) drawn from aqueous solvation theory. The counter skill now retains the compact-solute term, neutralizes only the lowest-confidence smiles_mid prior, and replaces the halogen rule with a hetero_none apolar penalty plus an unbranched bonus, while shifting more rank mass to the target-only anchor mid-run. All mechanism statements remain hypotheses; two eight-seed blocks cannot establish causality.
